paper_summary: de Lorgeril, Wyss and Orbulov (Periodica Polytechnica Mech. Eng. 2011) propose a mathematical description (modified Chesler-Cram peak function plus fifth-order polynomial) of the compressive engineering stress-strain curves of pressure-infiltrated aluminium matrix syntactic foams (Al99.5, AlSi12, AlMgSi1, AlCu5, AlZn5 matrices with 64 vol% Envirospheres SL150 or SL300 ceramic microballoons). 540 upsetting tests (three aspect ratios, three heat-treatment/temperature conditions) were fitted, and only qualitative trends of compressive strength, fracture strain, structural stiffness and absorbed energy versus H/D ratio are reported in the annex tables.
extraction_notes: FLAGGED FALSE PER RULE 10 (no quantitative hollow-particle composite data), although the subject IS metal matrix syntactic foam. The paper is clearly about metal matrix syntactic foams, but it reports NO numerical property values: compressive strength, fracture strain, stiffness and absorbed energy are shown only as trend words (increase/decrease/constant/hat/valley/unknown) in Tab. 4-7 and in unreadable Figs. 4-7. Therefore no records were created. Material descriptors available for future use: matrices Al99.5, AlSi12, AlMgSi1, AlCu5, AlZn5; microballoons Envirospheres SL150 (100 um average diameter, bulk density 0.576 g/cm3 at 64 vol%) and SL300 (150 um, 0.691 g/cm3 at 64 vol%), 30-35 wt% Al2O3 / 45-50 wt% amorphous SiO2 / 19 wt% mullite / 1 wt% quartz; 64 vol% microballoons in all cases; pressure infiltration; 14 mm diameter cylinders with H/D = 1, 1.5, 2; conditions ST 20 (solution treated, 20 C), HT 20 (T6, 20 C), ST 220 (solution treated, tested at 220 C); T6 parameters in Tab. 3. The 'Density (at 64 vol%)' column in Tab. 2 refers to the microballoon bed, not the foam.
